claims.text: Cast refractory multi-principal element alloys such as Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr-Cr can exhibit limited ductility associated with brittle Laves or other intermetallic phases.
Severe plastic deformation can reduce the target alloy's grain size below 50 nm.
SPD followed by low-temperature annealing will produce a nanocrystalline dual-phase BCC+B2 structure in the proposed refractory alloy system.
Annealing AlCoFeNi at 600 °C can decompose an ordered B2 phase into a fine-scale B2+BCC mixture.
An annealing range of 600–800 °C is sufficient to induce B2/BCC phase separation while remaining below the Laves- or sigma-phase nucleation threshold in the target refractory alloy.
Room temperature to 0.4 Tm is a suitable SPD processing-temperature range for achieving the proposed nanocrystalline structure.
Keeping oxygen below 0.8 wt% helps avoid oxide-associated hardening and embrittlement.
The dual-phase microstructure contains coherent interfaces between a nanocrystalline BCC matrix and fine B2/BCC precipitates.
A high grain-boundary density stabilizes the coherent BCC/B2 interfaces.
Short, low-temperature annealing suppresses brittle intermetallic formation by limiting the long-range diffusion needed for Laves or sigma nucleation and growth.
A grain size below 50 nm increases strength through Hall–Petch grain-boundary strengthening.
Atomic-size mismatch in a retained BCC solid solution contributes solid-solution strengthening.
Fine coherent precipitates contribute dispersion strengthening.
Brittle Laves and sigma phases generally require higher annealing temperatures or longer times than the proposed low-temperature anneal.
The processed material will attain hardness greater than 15 GPa, comparable to nanocrystalline W-Ta-V-Cr.
The processed material will have yield strength significantly above the as-cast baseline.
The processed material will retain fracture strain above 5% because continuous brittle intermetallic networks are absent and coherent interfaces impede crack propagation.
In CrMoNbWV, exceeding approximately 1200 °C causes the Laves-phase volume fraction to increase rapidly.
Oxygen above approximately 0.8 wt% can produce HfO2 particles, strong hardening, cracking, and embrittlement in an Hf-containing refractory alloy.
Some alloy compositions inherently form sigma phase at grain boundaries even at low temperatures.

contradictions.description: The predicted ductility criterion is fracture strain above 5%, but the experiment only treats fracture strain below 1% as falsifying. A result between 1% and 5% would violate the prediction without meeting the stated falsification rule.
